doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Recent CD 'Sax After Midnight' and its sales
summary: After playing a track, he discusses the CD's success, the sidemen, and the producer's studio additions.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Let me play a little selection for you here. This is one of your more recent efforts.
[audio interlude]
That’s some good late night music right there.
It’s doing very well too, which proves the melody sells.
The melody sells.
Yeah, the melody sells. It’s doing very big in Germany and mail order with this company, and England. They’re going to move it into Italy now too. No, you just play the melody very easy.
It’s got nice back-up too.
Yeah, right.
Nice musicians behind you there.
Yeah Linc Milliman, have you heard of him?
Yes, as a matter of fact he went to the college I went to.
Oh okay. He’s on the bass. So he plays beautiful. And Ed Shanaphy is the owner of the company but he played. He did all the doctoring up of it, and some additions to it.
Right. They do that after the fact?
Yeah.
You record as a quartet?

Right. Then he did surgery. Like “In The Wee Small Hours of the Morning” if you heard that, he put a town clock to that in the beginning, if you heard the introduction, which was nice because when I was a kid and we’d come home in Tarrytown, they had a town clock. And you’d come home at four in the morning and you’re like that, and it would ring. So when he did that it made me very happy.
That’s curious, you mentioned that it’s doing well overseas.
Yeah. Here too, they just got a big mail order company.
Maybe you should consider going overseas.
I would now, now I would. Because I’m clear, I could do what I want to do. But I don’t want to go — I wouldn’t go with a big band. Some people have been asking me about it.
